newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Maskhadov optimistic on Chechen independence.
newsitem.headline: Maskhadov optimistic on Chechen independence.

text.p: Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov said on Monday he was pleased with talks with Russian President Boris Yeltsin and said he had high hopes of negotiating formal independence for his breakaway republic.

"I think I was able to convince Boris Nikolayevich to put an end to our remaining problems," Maskhadov told reporters after the talks in Moscow. "I am very pleased with the meeting, because today I saw in Boris Nikolayevich a man who is really aware of the need to solve the problems of the last 400 years."

Maskhadov said he hoped a joint Chechen-Russian commission could begin work as early as next week on agreeing a final political settlement, an outline of which the Chechens had presented to Yeltsin on Monday.

He said he believed Yeltsin understood the Chechens' need for independence after their battle against Russia, which began under the tsars, and thought the Russian people were also prepared to recognise the region.

Russian news agencies earlier quoted Yeltsin as saying he was ready to negotiate a long-term political deal with Chechnya but made clear he still viewed the rebel region as an integral part of Russia.
Yeltsin suggested wide-reaching autonomy along the lines of that granted in 1994 to Tatarstan, a mainly Moslem republic, like Chechnya, on the Volga River in central Russia.
